newsitem.title: USA: U.S. property-casualty net up 32 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: U.S. property-casualty net up 32 pct in Q1.

text.p: The U.S. property-casualty insurance industry's consolidated after-tax net income rose 32.6 percent to $10.0 billion in the first quarter of 1997, according to figures released by industry trade groups.

The figures also showed an improvement in the industry's first quarter profitability to a rate of return of 15 percent, up from 12.8 percent a year ago, according to Sean Mooney, senior vice president at the Insurance Information Institute.
The improved results and profitability reflected a sharp decline in catastrophe losses and an increase in investment income.
However, Mooney said he is not optimistic about the outlook for the industry, citing the industry's slow revenue growth.
Earned premiums, he noted, increased by only 2.6 percent in the first quarter, down from an increase of 3.8 percent for the full year of 1996.
The figures were released by Insurance Services Offfice Inc and the National Association of Independent Insurers through the Insurance Information Institute.
They are consolidated estimates for the entire industry based on reports of insurers that account for 96 percent of the country's property-casualty business.
Without adequate growth in revenue, Mooney said, the industry is dependent on luck to show an improvement in earnings.

Apart from milder winter weather leading to lower catastrophe losses, the industry has benefited from record results in the equities markets, which have allowed the industry to show large realized capital gains in recent years, Mooney said.
But, Mooney said, the results showed that this well can eventually run dry. Realized capital gains fell 53 percent in the first quarter from an unusually high 1996 first quarter.
The figures also showed that first quarter net income included pretax operating income of $10.1 billion, up from $4.4 billion a year ago.

The pretax operating income included a pretax underwriting loss of $1.5 billion in the first quarter, down from a loss of $4.9 billion in the first quarter of 1996, and pretax net investment income of $11.4 billion, up 23.1 percent from $9.3 billion a year ago.

Catastrophe losses in the first quarter totaled only $900,000 compared with $2.6 billion in the year ago first quarter, according to Property Claim Services, a group that tracks the industry's insured losses.
As a result of the improved loss experience in the first quarter, the combined ratio was 101.2 percent, the best quarterly combined ratio for the industry since 1979.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
Most of that increase in the investment income, however, was due to large special dividends two property-casualty insurers received from affiliated life insurance companies.
Excluding these dividends, investment income in the first quarter was up 2.1 percent from a year ago.
Realized capital gains of $2.2 billion in the first quarter were down from $4.8 billion a year ago and 15.3 percent less than in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Net written premium for the first quarter totaled $69.0 billion, up 3.3 percent from $66.8 billion a year ago.
That compares with first quarter written premium growth of 3.4 percent in 1996 and full year written premium growth of 3.5 percent for 1996.
The industry's consolidated surplus, its assets minus liabilities, increased $9.9 billion or 3.8 percent to $266.3 billion as of March 31, 1997.
